text:
emily_support: :rotating_light: Escalation from ACME — intermittent 504s during tenant burst (09:12-09:30 PST). ~15% of requests returned gateway timeout. sample request id rQX-504-112. Customer seeing scale-related errors in gateway logs: 
```
upstream error: scaleup_timeout, controller: scale-controller, attempt=1
```
Need fast triage, customer is worried about SLA.

alex_chung: On it. Can you drop tenant id + an example curl and any recent deploys?

emily_support: Tenant: tenant-acme. Example curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -v` — gateway logs show queue growth then 504s. No deploys in last 24h.

trent_ops: I pulled autoscaler logs and cluster events. Quick findings: KEDA ScaledObject cooldown=300s, HPA minReplicas=0. KEDA triggers but HPA reconciliation lagging. Also cluster autoscaler added nodes but new nodes have taint `spot=true:NoSchedule` and our pod spec lacks matching toleration + nodeAffinity points at `dedicated=ml` nodepool — leads to pods Pending or landing on smaller nodes and taking longer to init (image pull + model warmup).
Commands I ran: `kubectl get scaledobject tenant-acme -n prod -o yaml` and `kubectl describe pods -n prod | grep Pending`.

sara_nguyen: I dug into the deployment template — we added tolerations for `spot=true:NoSchedule` but accidentally scoped them under the sidecar container in the helm chart (wrong path), so scheduler ignored them. Also nodeAffinity block was using `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` but selector key typo `dedicated: ml ` (extra space) so it didn't match. Small config issues but big impact for bursty scale.

trent_ops: So root cause = race: KEDA scaler fires, HPA stays at 0 until reconciliation, combined with taint/affinity misconfig -> pods stuck Pending or schedule to cold nodes -> scale-up timeout at gateway -> 504s. Also saw that one attempt to reserve Dedicated capacity failed with billing service 403 (auth token expired) so we couldn't fallback to reserved pool for this tenant.

emily_support: Customer asked for immediate mitigation. Options? Can we patch config temporarily or pin them to a smaller model while we fix infra? Billing team says they can't grant reserved capacity until auth is fixed (403).

sara_nguyen: I'll push an emergency patch: set ScaledObject `cooldownPeriod`->30s for tenant-acme and set HPA `minReplicas`->1 to avoid coldzero during bursts. I'll also correct tolerations/nodeAffinity in the helm chart and deploy to prod canary. Patch command: `kubectl patch scaledobject tenant-acme -n prod --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/cooldownPeriod","value":30}]'` then `kubectl scale deploy/tenant-acme-runtime --replicas=1 -n prod` for immediate relief. Doing it now in staging then prod.

auto-scaler-bot: scaledobject/tenant-acme cooldown changed from 300 to 30 by sara_nguyen at 2026-02-15T09:45:12Z

alex_chung: Follow-ups: 1) Add queue_length and request_latency into KEDA scalers so we trigger earlier, 2) Add a tiny prewarm replica for critical tenants or enable warm-pool, 3) Add CI lint to catch helm path/typo for tolerations/affinity. Also consider a fallback lightweight model route if scale fails.

emily_support: Customer accepted temporary mitigation. Creating ticket for postmortem + config change: default ScaledObject cooldown -> 30s for burst-prone tenants, and enforce minReplicas=1 policy for SLAs. Tagging @product-ops for rollout and @security for verifying billing auth token rotation schedule.

product-ops: acknowledged. We'll schedule rollout in the next maintenance window and track follow-up action items in the postmortem.

emily_support: Marking this thread resolved for customer update; keeping open for postmortem notes and RCA. :white_check_mark:
